title: A Tide for the Promise
premise: Sable Hartwell has kept her heart on a strict training schedule since her mother's death: rise at four, bake, count the register, never let anyone stay past the last train. For ten years, unsigned letters from a stranger in a coastal prison town have been her one indulgence—until the letter writer, marine salvager Jonah Reyes, is released and moves into the apartment above her failing café, not knowing she's the woman he's written to. As Sable's lease collapses and a predatory developer circles her block, she discovers Jonah's letters hid a confession: he took the fall for a crime committed by the developer's family, the same family whose buyout could erase her café. Choosing justice outside the law over the safety of silence, Sable and Jonah expose the truth at a public hearing, and on the night the last train leaves without her, she finally lets someone stay.
about_author: Coral Villalobos is a former line cook who spent a decade writing letters to an incarcerated cousin, an experience that taught her how much truth a person can fit between the lines. She lives in a small harbor town where she bakes bread on Sundays and insists the best love stories begin with someone staying for one more cup of coffee.

chapters.title: Proofing Hours
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At 4 a.m. she counts the register—three missed payments from losing the lease—and rehearses her creed that the heart is a trainable muscle. A developer's flyer appears under her door. Emotional beat: controlled dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Tenth Letter
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She rereads the unsigned letters she's kept in a flour tin, the one indulgence she permits herself, and writes a reply she never sends. The last train's whistle closes the night like a lock. Emotional beat: longing she refuses to name.

chapters.title: A Man with Salt in His Voice
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Released after ten years, he moves into the apartment above the café carrying a box of unsent replies and no idea the baker below is his correspondent. Emotional beat: fragile hope, fear of being known.

chapters.title: Flour and Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Alternating. First meetings: he helps when her mixer seizes; she feeds him leftover croissants and sends him upstairs before the last train, her rule stated like scripture. Emotional beat: attraction immediately fenced in.

chapters.title: The Lease and the Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The bank declines her extension; the developer, Marlowe Grant, offers a buyout with a smile that doesn't reach his eyes. Jonah overhears and goes very still. Emotional beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: What the Letters Never Said
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Alone upstairs, he nearly slips a letter under her door, then stops—his confession about the Grant family's crime is inside. Emotional beat: guilt pressing on the pen.

chapters.title: Sunday Closed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The café closes for the first Sunday in nine years; Jonah stays past the last train to fix her roof leak, breaking her rule without asking. She lets him. Emotional beat: the first crack in the muscle.

chapters.title: The Salvage Diver
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Flashback to the night ten years ago: he watched Marlowe's father dump contaminated drums off his salvage boat and took the blame to protect his dying brother from a second conviction. Emotional beat: buried truth surfacing.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Hunger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A farmers-market day, shared stalls, hands brushing over a cash box. Marlowe appears, and Jonah's reaction—flinching, cold—plants Sable's first question. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: The Flour Tin
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cleaning for a health inspection, Jonah sees the tin of letters and recognizes his own handwriting. He says nothing; she watches him say nothing. Emotional beat: mutual, silent recognition dawning.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Closing
chapters.summary: Alternating. After the last train, she lays a letter on the counter: 'Why didn't you sign them?' He confesses everything but the crime. Emotional beat: betrayal and relief tangled together.

chapters.title: The Buyout Deadline
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Marlowe raises his offer with a veiled threat about her health violations; the bank gives her two weeks. Jonah urges her to refuse. Emotional beat: pressure from every side.

chapters.title: Brother's Keepers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. His brother Theo, newly out himself, warns him to stay silent—the Grants buried witnesses before. Jonah realizes Sable is now a witness too. Emotional beat: protective fear.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Her late mother's old business partner, who testified for the Grants a decade ago, begs Sable to take the money and forget it. Sable hears her mother's caution in the plea. Emotional beat: the theme sharpened—loyalty vs. truth.

chapters.title: The Harbor Records
chapters.summary: Alternating. Together they pull tide charts, salvage logs, and a maintenance receipt that places the Grant boat at the dump site. Working side by side past midnight, the investigation becomes intimacy. Emotional beat: partnership, tender and dangerous.

chapters.title: Broken Rule, Broken Window
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The café is vandalized overnight; a note says 'Drop it.' Jonah wants to send her away on the morning train. She refuses. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Theo's Testimony
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Theo, facing a parole revocation, agrees to speak if Jonah takes the blame again. Jonah refuses—this time the truth must carry its own name. Emotional beat: breaking the family pattern.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating. At the county environmental review, Sable presents the records and Jonah testifies to what he saw ten years ago, surrendering his anonymity and his protection. Marlowe's composure cracks. Emotional beat: the climax—justice outside the law, spoken publicly.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The buyout collapses; an investigation opens; the bank, suddenly cooperative, grants a restructuring. But Jonah, expecting consequences, prepares to leave town quietly. Emotional beat: victory hollowed by impending loss.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He packs his box of letters and walks to the station as the lease clock runs out. Sable finds his unsent final letter—addressed to her, signed at last—on the counter. Emotional beat: the choice made visible.

chapters.title: Stay
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She runs to the platform, past the departing train, and says the thing she's trained her heart never to say: stay. He does. The café lights burn past closing for the first time. Emotional beat: surrender, earned.

chapters.title: A Tide for the Promise
chapters.summary: Alternating, one year later. The café thrives; the harbor is being cleaned; a new letter sits in the flour tin—signed, dated, and answered. On the night the last train passes, neither of them moves. Emotional beat: peace; the promise kept.
